mainEntity.name: How far in advance should I plan my succession?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ideally 2-5 years before exit. Building value, cleaning financials, documenting systems, and removing owner-dependency takes time — rushed exits usually sell at a discount. The matched adviser helps you start early so you maximise value and minimise tax on exit.

A buy-sell agreement is a binding contract between business co-owners that sets out what happens if one dies, is incapacitated, or exits. It is typically funded by insurance. Without one, you may end up in business with your partner's family or face a discounted forced sale. The matched adviser structures the agreement with your lawyer and insurer.

mainEntity.name: Can I access small-business CGT concessions on exit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Potentially — small-business CGT concessions can reduce or eliminate CGT on a business sale, but the conditions (active-asset test, $6m net-asset test, $2m turnover test) must be met. The matched adviser assesses your eligibility before exit and structures the transaction to preserve the concessions. Planning early is essential — these cannot be retrofitted.

mainEntity.name: How much does succession planning advice cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A business valuation is typically $2,000–$8,000; ongoing succession advisory is usually quoted as a fixed fee or monthly retainer. The matched adviser gives you a clear quote after reviewing your situation — the matching is free.

mainEntity.name: How quickly will a matched succession adviser contact me?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most matches are completed within 60 seconds of finishing the questionnaire. Your matched adviser will typically reach out within 2 hours, or you can call for immediate assistance to discuss your succession plans.

mainEntity.name: Can a succession adviser help with a family business handover?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The matched adviser structures intergenerational transfers — addressing fairness among siblings, ongoing involvement, and tax-efficient transfer of ownership — so the family business transitions smoothly without disputes.

Yes. The matching service is free for businesses. We are engaged by the accounting firms in our network, not by you. You are under no obligation to proceed with any matched adviser, and the matched firm gives you a clear quote before any work begins.

mainEntity.name: Can a succession adviser prepare my business for sale?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The matched adviser prepares vendor due-diligence materials, cleans your financials, structures earn-out and restraint terms, and coordinates with your lawyer and broker — so you command a premium rather than a discount at sale.

blocks.heading: Succession Planning — what we can help with
blocks.text: SPECIALIST NETWORKSuccession Planning — what we can help withBuilding the value storyA business that is valuable to a buyer is one that does not depend on the owner — recurring revenue, documented systems, clean financials, and a management layer. Our matched advisers help you build these attributes over the 2-3 years before exit so you can command a premium, not a discount. Succession is a multi-year project, not a last-minute transaction.Family succession vs external salePassing to family has different considerations (tax, fairness among siblings, ongoing involvement) than an external sale (vendor due diligence, earn-outs, restraint terms). Our matched advisers structure the transaction for your specific path — family, management buyout, trade sale, or listed exit — and manage the tax outcomes accordingly.Buy-sell agreementsIf you have co-owners, a buy-sell agreement funded by insurance ensures the business continues if a partner dies, is incapacitated, or exits. Without one, you may end up in business with your partner's spouse — or face a fire-sale at a discount. Our matched advisers structure buy-sell agreements and coordinate with your lawyer and insurer.
